newsitem.title: USA: Motorola rises on expected Japan contract.
newsitem.headline: Motorola rises on expected Japan contract.

text.p: Shares of technology giant Motorola Inc rose 1-7/8 to 59-1/4 on Tuesday amid expectation the company will announce a major contract with a Japanese wireless phone company.
The company's Cellular Infrastructure Group said it will hold a media briefing on Wednesday to announce "significant developments", but declined to give further details.
Analysts said the deal was likely for Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) technology with a major Japanese firm, and would be an important contract for Motorola.
"Motorola coming in (to the Japanese CDMA market) is huge," said John Lazlo, an analyst for PaineWebber, citing the expected deal as the reason behind the strength in the stock.
Motorola has been active in opening the Japanese telecommunications market to competition and already has deployed earlier wireless phone systems in Japan.

Analysts said a significant deal would also be a victory for CDMA, one of various competing technologies developed to expand wireless phone networks and enhance call quality. Japan recently adopted CDMA as a standard technology.
Hambrecht & Quist analyst Rakesh Sood pointed out that Motorola has invested heavily in CDMA while its key competitors Nokia Oy of Finland and Ericsson of Sweden have not.
"It is really significant for Motorola," Sood said. "Their traditional archrivals are not players there (in CDMA), so Motorola has a significant advantage from that point of view."
